# Quantum Magic Burst Routing

This project uses the source identity of noisy T states to assign their input
slots in a fixed magic-state distillation circuit. The source-error model,
proofs and hardware interface are explained in science/.

- README.md — question, principal results, learning, reproduction and contact.
- science/README.md — connected specialist reading route.
- science/model.md — ideal injection circuit, binary syndrome and parity,
  fault distributions, success convention and charged resources.
- science/routing.md — explicit five-source placement, complement classes,
  optimal syndrome information and the reliability–yield tradeoff.
- science/phase-tied-receivers.md — source phase ties, a parity receiver with
  the same burst decision frontier, projection cost and phase mismatch.
- science/noise.md — independent per-input faults, exact Walsh formulas and
  the minimum number of harmful whole-plus-partial burst patterns.
- science/scaling.md — punctured Reed–Muller family and balanced placement.
- science/scheduling.md — finite delivery, retry and interleaving comparison.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md — attribution and nearby operational models.
- references/references.bib — source metadata.
- learning/README.md — learning entry point.
- learning/MILESTONES.md — exactly 30 project-defined understanding targets.
- learning/GOTTESMAN_BRIDGE.md — single educational source and proof bridges.
- verification/README.md — commands and coverage of the runnable checks.

For the headline error law, follow the 15-slot construction in routing.md
and check the assumptions in model.md. For limitations and noise robustness,
read noise.md and scheduling.md. The whole-burst syndrome comparison applies
to a fixed ideal gadget, including unequal or dependent source histories.
The exact p-law assumes independent equally likely whole-source faults.
Independent per-slot faults change the comparison. Nothing here establishes
a hardware-independent cost reduction or fifth order under arbitrary noise.
